description:
## Goal

src/websocket/socket_manager.cr spawn_writer_fiber creates a
per-connection writer fiber. The fiber exits only when
conn.outgoing is closed, which happens in
handle_unregister_connection, handle_connection_closed,
handle_shutdown_all, and handle_cleanup_dead.

Risk: if HTTP::WebSocket#closed? returns false but the underlying
TCP socket is half-closed (NAT timeout, client crash, etc.),
the writer fiber is stuck on a blocking send, holding
conn.websocket, conn.outgoing, and any pending broadcast
payloads (which can be MB for big feeds).

## Approach

1. Wrap writer sends with a select + small timeout (e.g. 5s).
   On timeout, send a connection_send_error cast and break out
   of the loop (or close the outgoing channel so the fiber
   exits).
2. Periodic self-check: every N seconds the writer checks
   conn.websocket.closed? and exits if true (with a
   CastConnectionClosed message to clean up actor state).
3. Increase cleanup_dead frequency from on-demand to a periodic
   timer in the reporter (every 30s) so dead connections are
   reaped even when no new ones register.
4. Verify handle_register_connection's purge_closed_connections
   rolls back the IP count for the stale entries it purges
   (it currently does not increment on the new connection until
   after the purge, so this is fine — but check).

## Acceptance

- Writer fiber exits within 5s of a slow/dead client.
- cleanup_dead runs every 30s; connection_count and
  EventBroadcaster.client_count agree within one tick.
- No code path retains a Connection whose websocket has been
  closed for > 60s.
- Build + spec + ameba clean.
title: Cap SocketManager writer fiber lifetime + connection cleanup
